speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me determine the cause, please tell me how long these symptoms have been present.

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of pain relieved by voiding, accompanied by dyspareunia and no fever, is highly suggestive of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome, but I need to confirm if there is any visible blood in your urine or if you have had any recent urinary tract infections.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis Color: Clear, pH: 6.7, Specific_Gravity: 1.010, Protein: 1+, Glucose: Negative, Ketones: Negative, Blood: Negative, Nitrite: Negative, Leukocyte Esterase: Negative, WBC: 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells: 2/hpf, Bacteria: None

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis results are reassuring as they show no signs of infection, stones, or blood, which helps rule out a UTI or malignancy. To further investigate the bladder wall pathology, please perform a Cystoscopy with hydrodistension and biopsy.

REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy with hydrodistension
REQUEST IMAGES: Cystoscopy_photos

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cystoscopy Findings: Normal urethra and bladder mucosa

speaker: Doctor
text: The cystoscopy confirms a normal bladder mucosa, ruling out Hunner's ulcers or tumors; to further evaluate for microscopic hematuria, interstitial cystitis, or urethral pathology, I need to see the Cystoscopy photos and understand your specific pain characteristics. REQUEST IMAGES: Cystoscopy_photos. Can you describe if the pain is worse at the end of urination, and have you noticed any vaginal discharge or a history of STIs?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS). The diagnosis is supported by your chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, frequency, dyspareunia, sterile urinalysis, and normal cystoscopy.
